nodes.label: Adam Training Results (loss/accuracy curves)
nodes.rationale: Chart with Adam optimizer: fast convergence, training accuracy ~0.91 but validation plateaus ~0.86 and validation loss rises after ~40 epochs, indicating overfitting.

nodes.label: Dropout Effect Training Results
nodes.rationale: Chart showing that with dropout, validation loss stays at/below training loss (~0.29) and validation accuracy tracks training accuracy (~0.87): overfitting removed.

nodes.label: SGD Training Results (loss/accuracy curves)
nodes.rationale: Chart of training vs validation loss and accuracy over ~115 epochs with SGD optimizer: slow convergence, validation accuracy ~0.83 and noisy validation loss, training accuracy ~0.87.

nodes.label: Dropout Regularization
nodes.rationale: Applied to close the train/validation gap seen with Adam.

nodes.label: 1D Convolution on One-Hot DNA Diagram
nodes.rationale: Diagram: a 4x301 one-hot input is convolved with 27 filters (f0..f26) of size 4x4, producing 27 feature maps of length 298.

nodes.label: DNA Double Helix Illustration
nodes.rationale: Decorative header image: DNA double helix over a green 'matrix' code rain, evoking DNA as data for computation.

nodes.label: Max Pooling Diagram
nodes.rationale: Diagram: convolution outputs R0..Rn grouped in windows of 3 and reduced by max pool to R0'..Rn'.

nodes.label: One-Hot Encoding of DNA Sequence
nodes.rationale: Diagram: nucleotide sequence (C,G,A,T,...) encoded as a 4-row binary matrix, one row per base.

nodes.label: Receptive Field Diagram
nodes.rationale: Diagram (French labels): input of size 14 -> conv kernel 4 -> 11 -> max pool -> 4 -> conv kernel 4 -> 1 -> max pool -> 1, showing how stacked conv/pool layers grow the receptive field so one output sees the whole input.

nodes.label: Ambiguous / Multi-mapping Reads
nodes.rationale: Short ~50bp paired-end reads cannot be placed unambiguously on repeats, so they are usually discarded.

nodes.label: Hicberg
nodes.rationale: Repeated-sequence reads are filtered by standard NGS pipelines, creating white stripes and information loss; Hicberg uses statistical inference on unambiguous reads plus pseudo-random generators to reassign ambiguous reads.

nodes.label: Chaos Game Representation (CGR)
nodes.rationale: Maps DNA sequences onto a 2D square with nucleotides A,G,C,T at corners; recursive subdivision encodes k-mer frequencies as image pixels, enabling image-based CNNs on DNA.

nodes.label: DNA Sequence Gene-Family Classification (7 classes)
nodes.rationale: Class 6 dominates (~31%) in all three species while class 5 is smallest (5-7%), indicating class imbalance consistent across human, dog and chimpanzee.
